newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bouncy mark sets sights on 73.50 yen.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bouncy mark sets sights on 73.50 yen.

text.p: The mark is in high spirits after bouncing off the much-vaunted 72.50 yen support zone on Thursday, and is now set for a push to 73.50 and perhaps further, technical analysts said.
The 73.50 area represents a 50 percent retracement of the mark's decline from 74.35 to 72.65, said Nick Shamin, currency analyst at Technical Data here.

Above there, 61.8 percent of the same move cuts in at 73.65, where highs from late March and early April also cluster, Shamin noted. "That's a key resistance level, and that should stall it on the upside," he said.
Eddie Matts, director at Capital Management UK, said 73.60 was a key pivot.
"Though only above this level confirms a resumption of the medium-term uptrend for 74.30, short-term price action is very encouraging," said Matts.
The mark was quoted at 73.37/39 yen at 0848 GMT, up from late Thursday's European level of 73.10/15 and well above yesterday's intrasession low of 72.53.
Support intervenes at 73.20 -- site of hourly congestion and near recent daily highs -- ahead of today's low and a downward trendline around 72.95/73.00, chartists said.
